correctness.rationale: Exact Gram eigenvalues \(m\pm|S|\) give a singular set consisting of one point of the \((m-1)\)-torus. The local quadratic matrix \(B=I-\mathbf1\mathbf1^\mathsf T/m\) has eigenvalues \(1\) and \(1/m\), so the high-condition event is squeezed between ellipsoids of squared radius \(4m/t^2\); their Haar volumes produce the claimed constant. Tail integration proves the moment criterion, and the two-sample case admits direct exact trigonometric integration. The standalone code checks the rational determinant/phase identities and selected numerical consequences; these do not serve as proofs for unbounded sample count or threshold.

value.rationale: This natural minimal two-frequency random Fourier collocation problem has a complete sharp reliability classification for every sample count. The precise probability constant and moment threshold distinguish typical full rank from heavy-tail numerical sensitivity, show that two samples have infinite mean condition number, and quantify how each additional independent observation improves the rare-event exponent. The result is not a restatement of the source paper’s high-feature-count lower bound.
